title: Repo structure and conventions
routing: Is this about where code belongs or how we build here: the three packages (packages/core @inixiative/foundry-core, packages/foundry @inixiative/foundry, packages/acp @inixiative/foundry-acp) and their boundaries (core is primitives and pure data; providers, HTTP and processes stay in foundry; foundry-acp imports only @inixiative/foundry/client), the module import order (agents → providers → adapters → eval → viewer), licenses (MIT, BSL 1.1), the tech stack (Bun, strict TypeScript, bun test, BullMQ, Prisma/Postgres, SQLite), atlas (@atlas blocks with @kind / @partOf / @uses, .atlas/concepts.ts, bunx atlas stamp / query / graph / generate, atlas check at 100%), or the design principles and common mistakes (don't reinvent Claude Code, no backwards-compat shims, no opinions in core, no hand-named Wardens, Haiku on decisions)? Plain jobs: 'which package does this go in', 'can core import this', 'where is this concept in the code', 'I added a new file', 'is this allowed here'.
